title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression by IRLS and EM
text: Many outcomes health, social sciences industry counts: number doctor visits year, articles student publishes, defects production line. Poisson regression model natural starting point, forces variance equal mean. Real count data often overdispersed, variance much larger mean, can also contain zeros Poisson model mean can produce. Ignoring overdispersion gives standard errors small, ignoring excess zeros gives poor description zero count . negative binomial (NB2) model handles overdispersion adding dispersion parameter θ\theta, Var(Y)=μ+μ2/θ\mathrm{Var}(Y)=\mu+\mu^2/\theta. zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model goes treats data coming two processes: structural process produces zeros (example, people never see doctor), NB count process can also produce zeros. goal project R package, nbzinbPate, fits models estimation code written scratch. NB model fitted iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) regression coefficients, alternated Newton-Raphson log⁡θ\log\theta. ZINB model, whose likelihood generalized linear model, fitted EM algorithm whose M-steps IRLS fits. general-purpose optimizer (optim(), nlm(), …) GLM fitter (glm(), lm(), …) used. package checked MASS::glm.nb() pscl::zeroinfl(), studied simulation, applied physician office visits NMES1988 data.

title: Zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression — zinbreg
text: Fits ZINB model Lambert (1992) NB2 count component: $$P(Y_i = 0) = \pi_i + (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta), \quad       P(Y_i = y) = (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(y;\mu_i,\theta),\ y \ge 1,$$ \(\log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) (count model) \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\) (zero-inflation model). Estimation EM algorithm: E-step computes posterior probability \(\tau_i\) zero structural zero, M-step fits fractional-response logistic regression \(\gamma\) weighted NB regression (weights \(1-\tau_i\)) \((\beta,\theta)\), IRLS. general-purpose optimizer used. parameterization pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin").
